text: In India, when a two-wheeler tyre wears out, riders don't ask a dealer. They ask the mechanic down the road.
Eurogrip's own research shows mechanics know the brand, but rarely recommend it. Stock lags behind rivals, cash schemes fade, and mechanics now want tools and respect more than cash.
So we built Grip Guild. We don't pay mechanics. We make them more successful, with three things that compound: tools, customers, and status.
This is our live prototype: a FastAPI backend, a Next.js frontend, and eight personas you can actually play.
Meet Ravi. He runs a puncture shop and doesn't even stock Eurogrip. His Guild Coach shows what will grow his shop today.
Every verified fitment earns points, and half of them pay off a tyre changer he will own. Scan the same tyre twice, and Fraud Guard blocks it.
When Priya, a delivery rider, gets a flat, Puncture SOS finds the nearest Guild shop. Ravi accepts, and she sees his arrival time instantly.
No stock? Ghost Shelf lets Ravi sell Eurogrip anyway, delivered by the dealer within hours, and referral codes reward his word alone.
Every fitted tyre gets a 3D digital twin, with a wear heatmap, history, and a genuine-tyre check.
And Eurogrip sees it all: the funnel, fraud alerts, and true lift against control districts, while Budget Autopilot moves money to what works.
What makes it different? It rewards influence without inventory, turns advocacy into owned tools, and sends mechanics customers instead of cash.
Our simulator projects thirty-five thousand active shops and nearly nine lakh extra tyres in year one, at about two hundred and eighty rupees each.
It fits the brief's budget, runs on Eurogrip's existing dealers and field force, and the pilot can start in eight weeks.
Grip Guild. Tools, customers, status. Built by Team Outliers.
